artifacts.summary: Confirms cslib-research-agent.md has no terminal-metadata stage at all (root cause of the research_complete incident), specifies mirrored Stage 7 text with artifacts-shape rationale for all three cslib agents, and settles the .orchestrator-handoff.json question as an explicit prohibition for the two non-hard agents and a two-gap fix (continuation_context->continuation_path, artifacts rationale) for the hard agent, per the now-completed handoff-unification and cslib summary-format prerequisite tasks.

memory_candidates.content: When an agent's Stage 0 writes 'status: in_progress' but the file has no terminal Stage 7/final-metadata section, agents fabricate off-vocabulary status values (observed: 'research_complete') at return time rather than failing loudly. The fix is always additive: insert an explicit terminal-metadata stage naming the exact allowed status string(s) from return-metadata-file.md's normative vocabulary, plus the artifacts array-of-objects shape with its bare-string-array-breaks-.artifacts[0].path rationale, mirrored from general-research-agent.md's Stage 7 near-verbatim rather than paraphrased, to keep future drift-detection greppable.

handoff-schema.md's 'Handoff Writers' table is the single settled source for whether an agent may write .orchestrator-handoff.json: it is formally hard-mode-implement-only. Research agents (any mode) and base-mode (non-hard) implementation agents must never write it -- they return exclusively via .return-meta.json. When auditing or fixing an extension's agent files for handoff-contract compliance, check this table first rather than inferring the rule from an individual agent file's existing (possibly wrong) behavior.
